chain.label: FAA oversight of Part 91 revenue passenger-carrying operations inadequate
chain.trigger: the Federal Aviation Administration's inadequate oversight of Title 14 Code of Federal Regulations Part 91 revenue passenger-carrying operations

chain.label: Deficient safety management at Liberty and NYONair; Liberty ceded operational control
chain.trigger: Liberty's and NYONair's deficient safety management, which did not adequately mitigate foreseeable risks associated with the harness/tether system interfering with the floor-mounted controls and hindering passenger egress

chain.label: Floor-mounted fuel shutoff lever unprotected from external influences
chain.trigger: The certification basis for the accident helicopter's FSOL did not require protection from inadvertent activation due to external influences, such as interference from a passenger.

chain.label: Unsecured tether tail of front passenger's harness/tether system dangling into floor-mounted controls
chain.trigger: each time he leaned back, the tail of the tether attached to the back of his harness hung down loosely near the helicopter's floor-mounted controls

caused_by.evidence: Ineffective safety management at both companies allowed foreseeable safety risks to remain unmitigated; these included the potential for passenger interference with the helicopter's floor-mounted controls
exploitation of the aerial work/aerial photography exception at 14 CFR 119.1(e) to operate FlyNYON flights under Part 91 with limited FAA oversight

chain.label: Harness/tether release means (locking carabiners, ineffective cutting tools) not rapidly releasable
chain.trigger: minimally trained passengers would have great difficulty extricating themselves from the harness/tether system, each of which was equipped with locking carabiners and an ineffective cutting tool, during an emergency requiring a rapid egress

caused_by.evidence: Liberty Helicopters Inc.'s and NYONair's decision to use locking carabiners and ineffective cutting tools as the primary means for passengers to rapidly release from the harness/tether system was inappropriate and unsafe.

chain.label: Float system junction box installed aft of prescribed location, producing high activation-handle pull forces
chain.trigger: the junction box for the activation handle's pull cable was installed on the outboard side of the left frame rail about 1.6 inches farther aft and about 0.25 inch higher than the location prescribed

chain.label: No published activation-handle pull-force limitation; FAA certification review missed the omission
chain.trigger: In the absence of information from Dart Aerospace specifying pull-force limitations for the emergency flotation system's activation handle, Liberty and other operators lack a means to inspect for and correct high pull forces

chain.label: Tether tail caught on FSOL and pulled it to the shutoff position when passenger repositioned
chain.trigger: He noticed the tail of the front passenger's tether had caught on the FSOL and pulled it up.

caused_by.evidence: the tail of his tether remained taut but appeared to pop upward. Two seconds later, the helicopter's engine sounds decreased
lack of protection from inadvertent activation of the helicopter's fuel shutoff lever

chain.label: Fuel shutoff valve closed, interrupting fuel flow to the engine
chain.trigger: Moving the FSOL to the up position closes the fuel shutoff valve to stop fuel flow to the engine

caused_by.evidence: inadvertent activation of the FSOL, interruption of fuel flow to the engine

chain.label: Loss of engine power in cruise at 1,900 ft msl
chain.trigger: lost engine power during cruise flight

caused_by.evidence: interruption of fuel flow to the engine, and loss of engine power

chain.label: Pilot stopped short of full activation-handle travel, believing the floats were fully deployed
chain.trigger: the high forces required to pull the activation handle, along with the aural and visual cues following a single-reservoir discharge, led the pilot to mistakenly believe that he had successfully pulled the handle fully aft to fully inflate the floats

caused_by.evidence: once he felt sure that the helicopter could reach the river, he activated the emergency float system
a force of about 45 lbs on the activation handle was required before the left reservoir assembly activated
neither the RFMS nor any of Dart's installation, maintenance, or inspection instructions ... contained any information about activation handle pull-force limitations

chain.label: Only the left gas reservoir discharged; floats inflated partially and asymmetrically
chain.trigger: the left valve had activated, and the right valve had not

caused_by.evidence: contrary to the accident pilot's belief, the investigation found that the handle had not been pulled through its full travel. As a result, the valve on only the left gas reservoir assembly was activated.

chain.label: Autorotative descent and ditching on the East River
chain.trigger: the pilot performed an autorotative descent and ditching on the East River in New York, New York

caused_by.evidence: the helicopter was too low to allow engine power to be restored in time to prevent the emergency landing

chain.label: Helicopter rolled right, capsized, and became fully inverted and submerged
chain.trigger: within about 11 seconds of touchdown, the helicopter was completely inverted and submerged with only the floats visible above the surface

caused_by.evidence: after the helicopter touched down upright on the water, it immediately began to list then roll to the right
the rapid capsizing of the helicopter due to partial inflation of the emergency flotation system

chain.label: Five passengers unable to egress and drowned; pilot escaped with minor injuries
chain.trigger: The pilot sustained minor injuries, the five passengers drowned, and the helicopter was substantially damaged.

caused_by.evidence: the helicopter's rapid capsizing reduced the amount of time available for egress before the cabin became submerged
the NYONair-provided harness/tether system contributed to the passenger fatalities because it did not allow the passengers to quickly escape from the helicopter
